title: Pronunciation is regular
description: Basque is written as it is pronounced; these digraphs matter.
rows: here (h is silent in the south)

title: Personal pronouns
description: Basque pronouns have no gender and change form by case.

title: izan (to be) — present
description: izan expresses identity or essence: what something is.

title: egon (to be) — present
description: egon expresses a state or a location: how or where something is.

title: eduki (to have) — present
description: The transitive auxiliary agrees with both subject and object.

title: The article -a / -ak
description: Basque marks 'the' with a suffix, not with a separate word.

title: Negation with ez
description: ez goes immediately before the auxiliary verb.

title: Question words
description: The question word comes first and the verb keeps its normal place.

title: Demonstratives
description: There are three distances, as in Spanish.

title: Numbers 1–20
description: Numbers stay unchanged before the noun.

title: Possessives
description: nire, zure, haren… also take the article with the noun.

title: The cases at a glance
description: Basque marks the role of a noun with suffixes; this is the core of the language.
rows: I have given it to him.
Se lo he dado a él.

title: Inessive -n (non: where)
description: The ending -n answers 'where?' for being in a place.

title: Allative -ra (nora: where to)
description: The ending -ra answers 'where to?'.

title: Ablative -tik (nondik: where from)
description: The ending -tik answers 'where from?'.

title: Comitative -rekin (with)
description: The ending -rekin means 'with' or 'together with'.

title: Days of the week
description: Days take the article and are not capitalised.

title: Basic word order
description: Basque is Subject–Object–Verb, and time expressions go before the verb.

title: The ergative -k
description: The subject of a transitive verb takes -k: ni → nik, zu → zuk, hura → hark.

title: The dative -ri (nori)
description: The dative marks the person something is given or said to.

title: gustatu (to like)
description: The person who likes takes the dative and the thing liked is the subject.

title: izan — past
description: The past of izan is used for identity in the past.

title: eduki — past
description: The past auxiliary agrees with the object as well as the subject.

title: Habitual aspect (-tzen / -ten)
description: The habitual form describes what one does regularly.

title: Progressive: -tzen ari naiz
description: ari + the auxiliary expresses an action happening now.

title: Future -ko / -go
description: The future is formed with the participle plus -ko / -go.

title: behar, nahi and ahal
description: These modals follow the main verb in its participle form.
rows: I do not want to go

title: Postpositions
description: Location words follow the noun, which takes the genitive -en.

title: Comparison and superlative
description: baino + -ago compares; -en forms the superlative.
rows: Este es más grande que aquel.
This is as big as that.
Este es tan grande como aquel.

title: Purpose -tzeko / -tzera
description: -tzeko means 'in order to'; -tzera is used with verbs of movement.
rows: I am going to the shop to buy
voy a la tienda a comprar

title: Cause with -lako
description: -lako attaches to the verb and means 'because'.
rows: I am not coming because I am working.
He does not buy it because it is expensive.
No lo compra porque es caro.
I am happy because I have holidays.
I am at home because it is raining.
Estoy en casa porque está lloviendo.

title: Conditionals
description: ba- marks a real condition; the -n form plus nuke marks an unreal one.
rows: Euria egiten badu, ez gara joango.
If it rains, we will not go.
If you come, I will be happy.
Diru gehiago izango banu, bidaiatuko nuke.
If I had more money, I would travel.
Zu ni bazina, zer egingo zenuke?
If you were me, what would you do?

title: Plural transitive forms
description: When the object is plural, the auxiliary changes: ditut, dituzu, ditu…

title: Past habitual (-tzen nuen)
description: The habitual participle plus a past auxiliary means 'used to'.
rows: I used to go to school

title: Complement with -la
description: -la turns a clause into the object of verbs like 'to say' or 'to think'.
rows: I think that it is true.
He told me that he would come.
I know that they are difficult.
I thought that it was true.

title: Relative clauses with -en
description: The verb of a relative clause takes -en before the noun.
rows: Etorri den gizona nire laguna da.
The man who came is my friend.
El hombre que vino es mi amigo.
Zuk irakurri duzun liburua ona da.
The book that you read is good.
El libro que lees es bueno.
Atzo ikusi nuen etxea handia zen.
The house that I saw yesterday was big.
La casa que vi ayer era grande.
Hemen bizi den artzaina ezagutzen dut.
I know the shepherd who lives here.
Conozco al pastor que vive aquí.

title: Nominalising with -tzea
description: -tzea turns a verb into a noun, like the English -ing form.

title: Temporal -nean
description: -nean means 'when' and attaches to the past verb.
rows: Etxera iritsi nintzenean, lo egin nuen.
When I arrived home, I slept.
When you came, I was happy.
When the sun came out, we went.
Hura umea zenean, hor bizi zen.
When he was a child, he lived there.

title: Past indirect objects
description: The past auxiliary also marks who receives the action.
rows: Le di el libro a él.
Hark guri gauza bat kontatu zigun.

title: Instrumental -z
description: The ending -z marks the means, the vehicle or the language used.
rows: He wrote the book in Basque.

title: Partitive -rik
description: In negative sentences the object often takes -rik.

title: Concessive arren
description: arren after a participle means 'although'.
rows: Although I was tired, I came.
Hotz egin arren, ez ginen geratu.
Although it was cold, we did not stay.
Aunque hacía frío, no nos quedamos.
Although he is young, he is wise.
Dirurik ez izan arren, pozik dago.
Although he has no money, he is happy.
Aunque no tiene dinero, es feliz.

title: Postpositions with the genitive
description: Many postpositions need the noun in the genitive or dative.

title: Causal bait-
description: The prefix bait- marks a reason inside the sentence.
rows: I am not coming, because I am ill.
We will not buy it, because it is expensive.
No lo compraremos, porque es caro.
I am happy, because I have holidays.
We are not angry, because we agree.
No estamos enfadados, porque estamos de acuerdo.

title: Reported speech
description: Statements take -la, questions are kept inside, commands take -tzeko.
rows: He said that he would come.
He asked me where I lived.
He said that he would not come.

title: Potential: naiteke, zaitezke…
description: The potential form expresses 'can' as an ability or possibility.

title: Negative complement -enik
description: After a negated main verb, the subordinate verb takes -enik.
rows: I do not think that it is true.
I do not think that he will come.
I do not know that he is here.
No sé que él esté aquí.
I do not think that it is necessary.

title: -nez gero (since)
description: -nez gero gives the reason for what follows.
rows: Since you have come, I will help you.
Ya que has venido, te ayudaré.
Euria egiten duenez gero, etxean geratuko gara.
Since it is raining, we will stay at home.
Como está lloviendo, nos quedaremos en casa.
Since you have time, read this.
Ya que tienes tiempo, lee esto.
Hura hemen denez gero, hitz egingo diogu.
Since he is here, we will talk to him.
Ya que está aquí, hablaremos con él.

title: hain…non / ezen (so…that)
description: hain intensifies and non / ezen introduce the consequence.
rows: Hain da altua, ezen ez da sartzen.
He is so tall that he does not fit.
Es tan alto que no entra.
Hain zen hotza, non ez ginen atera.
It was so cold that we did not go out.
Hacía tanto frío que no salimos.
Hain da ona, non denek maite dute.
He is so good that everyone loves him.
Es tan bueno que todos lo quieren.
Hain zegoen nekatuta, ezen lo egin zuen.
He was so tired that he slept.

title: bezain / bezain laster
description: bezain compares equality; bezain laster means 'as soon as'.
rows: I am as tall as you.
This is as expensive as that.
Esto es tan caro como eso.
Hura ikusi bezain laster, pozik jarri nintzen.
As soon as I saw him, I became happy.
En cuanto lo vi, me puse contento.
Etxera iritsi bezain laster, lo egin nuen.
As soon as I arrived home, I slept.
En cuanto llegué a casa, dormí.

title: ezik (but rather)
description: ezik corrects or contrasts: 'not… but rather'.
rows: Lan egin ezik, atseden hartu zuen.
Ez dut kafea ezik tea nahiago dut.
I do not want coffee but rather tea.
Hura ez da medikua ezik irakaslea da.
He is not a doctor but a teacher.
Hemen ez da hotz ezik bero egiten du.
Here it is not cold but hot.
Aquí no hace frío, sino calor.

title: ala and ala ez
description: ala offers alternatives in questions; ala ez means 'whether or not'.
rows: Do you want coffee or tea?
Will you come today or tomorrow?
Etorriko zaren ala ez galdetu zidan.
He asked me whether you would come.
Me preguntó si vendrías o no.
Egia den ala ez ez dakit.
I do not know whether it is true.
No sé si es verdad o no.

title: -tzat (as, for)
description: -tzat means 'as' or 'for': hartu/jotu tzat.
rows: They consider that to be true.
Diru hori mailegu tzat hartu nuen.
I took that money as a loan.
I have a gift for you.

title: Resultant state -tuta / -ta
description: The participle with -ta describes the state left by an action.
rows: The books are placed on the table.
Los libros están puestos sobre la mesa.

title: -lakoan (thinking that)
description: -lakoan means 'believing / assuming that'.
rows: I was thinking that he would come.
Thinking the sun would come out, I went out.
Pensando que saldría el sol, salí.
Thinking I had time, I was calm.
Pensando que tenía tiempo, estaba tranquilo.
I was thinking that he was ill.

title: -en arabera (according to)
description: The genitive plus arabera means 'according to'.
rows: Depending on the weather, we will go.
According to the rules, that is forbidden.
Según las normas, eso está prohibido.
According to the data, the price has risen.
Según los datos, el precio ha subido.
According to what he says, it is true.
Según lo que él dice, es verdad.

title: baita ere / ez ezik…ere
description: baita ere adds; ez ezik…ere means 'not only… but also'.
rows: Hura etorri zen, eta zu baita ere.
Kafea gustatzen zait, baita ere tea.
I like coffee, and tea as well.
Me gusta el café, y el té también.
Hura ez ezik, zu ere etorri zara.
Not only he, but you too have come.
No solo él, tú también has venido.
Liburuak ez ezik, egunkariak ere irakurtzen ditut.
I read not only books but also newspapers.
Leo no solo libros sino también periódicos.

title: hainbat / batzuk
description: hainbat means 'several'; batzuk means 'some'.
rows: Some are books, the others magazines.
Algunos son libros, los otros revistas.
Some will come, the others not.
